data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The large service has direct control over its internal redundancy, while decentralization cannot enforce internal redundancy levels.","Decentralized network operators often have different threat models and budgets, whereas a single large service has a unified threat model.","The large service can internalize the cost of redundancy, while decentralized operators may externalize it."],"overturn_conditions":["Evidence that component failure, not control-plane failure, is the dominant failure mode in both systems.","Evidence that the large service's control plane is independently redundant to the same degree as the decentralized network's control planes.","Evidence that the decentralized network shares a common control plane (e.g., a shared orchestration layer)."],"shared_structure":["Both systems have a fixed total number of redundant components (N).","Both systems are vulnerable to correlated failure if a shared cause affects multiple components.","The difference in resilience hinges on the independence of the control plane, not the count of redundant components."],"source_memory_refs":["eb4515296f5292fab30875a85afa5f21db8fbdea9615468bb2d07d0cc19c62e2"],"transfer_claims":["If the large service's control plane fails, all N components are lost. If a decentralized service's control plane fails, only N/M components are lost.","The decentralized network's resilience is a function of the independence of its control planes, not the total count of redundant components.","The 'strictly more redundancy' condition is a red herring if the dominant failure mode is control-plane coordination."]},"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services is more resilient to correlated failure than one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy, provided that the dominant failure mode is control-plane coordination rather than component failure. The 'strictly more redundancy' condition is a mathematical trap if the failure probability is dominated by the control plane.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure mode is dominated by component failure rather than control-plane coordination.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service has a single, highly robust control plane with no single point of failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized services share a common control plane (e.g., a shared orchestration layer).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'strictly more redundancy' condition includes redundancy in the control plane itself, not just components.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A large service with N redundant components has N points of failure. A decentralized network with M services each having N/M redundancy has M*(N/M) = N points of failure, but distributed across independent control planes. If the failure probability is dominated by the control plane rather than the components, the decentralized network is always more resilient regardless of total redundancy counts.
